title: Single-library chromosome-scale diploid assemblies of vole genomes resolve a species-specific duplication implicated in pair bonding.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: NCBI Assembly records (esummary): 4 chromosome-level haplotype assemblies submitted 2026-07-04 — GCA_984569965.1/GCA_984569945.1 (prairie vole hap1/hap2, contig N50 39.2/51.0 Mb) and GCA_984569935.1/GCA_984569955.1 (meadow vole hap1/hap2, contig N50 46.5/43.6 Mb). Did not download the ~2.3 Gbp FASTA files (over the 50 MB cap).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only (no full text or supplement reachable through paper_context; Europe PMC flags it open access under PMC13277934 but no text was retrieved). The Avpr1a duplication, the Y-chromosome divergence and the HiFi+CiFi single-library method come from the abstract.

a1_downloadable.note: Four public GenBank assemblies exist (checked the NCBI Assembly metadata); the raw reads would be in SRA but are off-limits.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The data are genome sequences with no measured outcome. Any label (pair-bonding behaviour, gene copy number) would have to be constructed, and there are only two species.

a3_inputs_present.note: The sequences are present as FASTA in the assemblies (from NCBI metadata; files not opened).

a4_units_stated.note: There is no quantitative label, so there are no units.

a5_enough_rows.note: 4 haplotype assemblies from 2 species. Behaviour is a species-level trait, so effectively n=2.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~2.3 Gbp per haplotype, ~0.7 GB gzipped FASTA each (estimated)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Moot, because A2 and A5 fail.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The abstract describes diploid assemblies of 2 species, which matches the 4 haplotype assemblies on NCBI.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer or AlphaGenome (DNA language models), only hypothetically

honest_claim_h3: No supervised claim is possible: two species' genome assemblies with no per-item measured outcome.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use genome sequence differences between two vole species to predict which ones underlie monogamous pair-bonding behaviour.
plain_idea.train_on: Four haplotype genome assemblies (two per species) from prairie and meadow voles; 4 genomes in total, verified on NCBI.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a species pair-bonds. The only 'truth' is behaviour observed at the species level, so there are just 2 labelled units.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Vole social-behaviour labs would value it, but with two species there is nothing to learn statistically; the paper's value is as a reference genome resource.

label_elsewhere.sources: None relevant; the behavioural phenotype is species-level and known for only a handful of Microtus species.
label_elsewhere.why: No external labelled set exists to support a model.

ml_idea: None viable. At most, the assemblies could serve as test genomes for a sequence model, such as checking DNA-language-model gene annotation on a new rodent, but that is a different project with its labels elsewhere.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count labelled units: 2 species, so it is dead.

verdict_reason: Genome-assembly resource (4 haplotypes, 2 species) with no label column; A2 and A5 fail because any outcome would be a constructed species-level trait with n=2.
